S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

symptom.disease_info: Adjustment Disorder involves the development of emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable psychosocial stressor, emerging within about three months of the event and causing marked distress or functional impairment that is out of proportion to what would typically be expected. The disturbance is time-limited, usually resolving within six months after the stressor or its consequences end, and does not meet full criteria for another mental disorder such as major depressive disorder or PTSD. Clinically, patients often present with a clear narrative linking their difficulties to recent changes or stressors in relationships, work, health, or life transitions, and with noticeable decline in social, occupational, or academic functioning. It is differentiated from normal stress reactions by the degree of impairment and from other disorders by its temporal relationship to a stressor and subthreshold symptom patterns.

patient.stressor: About three months ago, Ariel’s husband was diagnosed with early-stage Parkinson’s disease after a winter of subtle motor changes that they had both been downplaying. As the more medically literate and organized partner, she quickly took on responsibility for coordinating his specialist appointments, researching treatment options, and driving him to physical therapy, all while trying to keep up with a major quality audit at her manufacturing plant. Her usual outlets—weekend hikes with the Cascade Trailblazers, evenings at the Seattle Repertory Theatre, and long knitting sessions—were increasingly pushed aside for caregiving tasks and extra hours at work to cover time missed for medical visits. Over the next two months, she noticed her attention to detail slipping during inspections, began making avoidable errors in SOP revisions, and started skipping yoga and club hikes, which alarmed both her supervisor and hiking friends; after a tense performance review and a worried comment from a close friend at bridge night, she agreed to see her primary care provider, who referred her for psychiatric evaluation when it became clear how overwhelmed she felt by the health changes at home.
patient.chief_complaint: Ever since my husband’s diagnosis, I feel like I’m reacting to everything in a way I can’t manage, and it’s starting to interfere with how I function at work and at home.

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.
S081.manifestation: Since my husband got the Parkinson’s diagnosis, it’s like a switch flipped and I overreact to everything—I’m snapping at coworkers over small mistakes, crying in the car after his appointments, lying awake running through worst-case scenarios instead of sleeping, and I’ve pretty much stopped doing the hikes and yoga that used to keep me grounded because I just feel too wound up and guilty to enjoy any of it.

add_requirements.symptoms_within_3_months_of_stressor: Within a few weeks of my husband getting the Parkinson’s diagnosis, I noticed myself becoming unusually irritable, tearful after his appointments, and too keyed up to enjoy my usual hikes or sleep properly.
add_requirements.resolve_within_6_months_after_stressor_e: I keep telling myself that once we get through this initial round of appointments and settle into a routine with his treatment, I’ll be able to get back to my normal schedule and feel more like myself again.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: My concentration has slipped so much that my supervisor had to call me in over several errors in my inspection reports, and at home I’ve withdrawn from my hiking group and yoga class, which used to be a big part of my social life and stress relief.
add_requirements.duration: These reactions have been building and bothering me for about the last two months, ever since the first wave of specialist visits and treatment planning after his diagnosis.
